pr.title: feat(prime): support Docker Compose task stacks on Prime VMs
pr.body:
The Prime provider from #3377 rejects Docker Compose tasks. This adds CPU Compose support: one Prime VM hosts the full stack, and Docker Compose handles service networking, DNS, health checks, builds, and volumes.

This is needed for running Harbor Compose tasks on Prime, including sidecar evidence collection and isolated grading, without implementing provider-specific Compose orchestration in downstream clients.

The implementation reuses `DinDComposeOps` and `ComposeServiceOpsMixin`. Provider code supplies host command/file transport and stack startup; Harbor's existing Trial runner owns collection, grading, and cleanup. No shared environment or agent interfaces change.

- Accept task Compose files and additional overlays, with Dockerfile builds or prebuilt service images.
- Keep main-service user, working directory, and environment settings separate from VM-host operations; preserve literal dollars in task environment values. Resolve Compose interpolation once into a mode-0600 config on the VM so subsequent Compose command requests do not forward task credentials.
- Apply Harbor's log/artifact mounts after authored files and extra overlays, preserving non-root writability even when task volumes target the same paths. Reject `docker-compose.yml` explicitly with the required `.yaml` filename.
- Use a configurable `compose_host_image` (default `python:3.11-slim-trixie`), installing Docker/Compose when absent. CPU and memory requests size the whole VM; Compose GPUs are unsupported.
- Bootstrap/build/pull with network access, then apply the task's Prime network policy before starting any service (`up --no-build --pull never`). As with the existing Prime provider, later policy changes affect new connections only.

Validation on real Prime VMs:

- Six live validation cases: shared oracle grading, isolated oracle grading, isolated no-op grading, startup deny-all policy, startup hostname allowlist, and the existing single-container lifecycle/transfer/network test. Startup
